sections.caption: I’m John Newsom. This is Information Assurance and Security. Watch this before you touch a lab — it covers the two questions that drive every assignment in this course, the four Texas clients you’ll work with, how a module is structured, and where to get help.

sections.html: Complete these 5 checkpoints in order before diving into assignments. Each step ensures you’re set up for success.

sections.label: ✓ 1. Read the Syllabus
paragraphs: The syllabus is your contract for grading, policies, and expectations. It covers late work policy, drop policies, academic integrity, and everything else that governs this course. Find it in your Canvas course navigation (usually labeled “Syllabus” in the left sidebar).

sections.label: ✓ 2. Obtain the Textbook
paragraphs: Required: Conklin & White, Principles of Computer Security: CompTIA Security+ and Beyond, Sixth Edition (ISBN: 9781260474312). McGraw-Hill Education.
items: UT San Antonio Bookstore — Physical or digital copies available
Amazon / other retailers — ISBN lookup for used copies; ensure 6th edition

image.alt: Cover of Principles of Computer Security, 6th Edition by Conklin and White

sections.label: ✓ 3. Join Discord (Optional but Recommended)
paragraphs: Discord is the fastest way to get help in this course. Most questions are answered within minutes by classmates or the instructor. You must read the Terms of Service before joining.

sections.label: ✓ 4. Complete Lab 1.0: Document Standards
paragraphs: Lab 1.0 is your first graded Training Lab and the first deadline in this course: Sunday, January 24 at 11:59 p.m. Central. It looks like a Word tutorial and it is not. Automatic tables of contents, captions and cross-references, and managed citations are the mechanics every Engagement Packet you write this term depends on.

It is technically droppable and you should not drop it. Students who skip past this lab spend the rest of the semester hand-typing things Word will build for them, and losing points for it. Do it first, before you touch the VM. Open it here: Lab 1.0: Document Standards.

sections.label: ✓ 5. Start Lab 1.1
paragraphs: Check your computer first. The Information Systems and Cybersecurity department requires you to own a laptop that meets its minimum device requirements, and Lab 1.1 depends on it. If you don’t have access to one, start with the options on that page, including the one-time financial aid adjustment for technology. Then email me on day one at john.newsom@utsa.edu so we can get you sorted as soon as possible. Don’t wait until Lab 1.1 is due.

Your Kali Linux VM is your security workstation for the entire semester. Setup happens inside Lab 1.1, so don’t set it up separately. Lab 1.1 walks you through installation, the VM naming convention, and the screenshot rules you’ll need for every assignment going forward. Lab 1.1 is due Sunday, January 31 at 11:59 p.m. Central. Open it here: Lab 1.1: Kali Environment Setup.

VM naming convention: Name your VM <your abc123>. Your abc123 is the ID you use to log into Canvas (for example, aaa000), and give Kali the same hostname, not your Banner ID number. This name must be visible in every screenshot. Lab 1.1 explains why.

sections.label: What’s Next?
sections.html: After completing all 5 checkpoints, head to Module 1: Threat Intelligence & Reconnaissance to begin your NEXUS journey.
Questions? Check How to Get Help or post in Discord. Don’t wait until you’re stuck. Ask early.
